analysis:
Only CHANGELOG.md changed: the v0.10.3 candidate section is retitled as published and a v0.10.4 candidate section is added (patch hunk @@ -8,9 +8,167, head lines 11-171). No executable code, configuration or protocol definitions are in this batch, so the source behaviour behind the claims was not examined.

The notes describe provider behaviour changes that touch the retained threat model, and the next pass should check them against the real source:
- Delta complete checkpoints for the SSD prefix cache (T-041, TB-007). The note says namespace binding to the binary and metallib hashes is unchanged, and that a 0.10.3 reader refuses delta files. The delta-file AAD and HMAC lookup-tag construction, and the rule that nothing prompt-derived is stored beyond the keyed tag, should be checked in SSDBlockStore and the checkpoint writers.
- Add-on hold hardening (TB-012, T-059, T-060). Claims: the signer is verified before the connection takes one of its 8 slots, a request line must finish within 10 seconds, and FIFOs at the hold record and mailbox paths are refused instead of blocking reads. The accept-time peer check, the timeouts and the fail-open hold record should be checked in the source.
- Re-registration of a provider the coordinator keeps refusing (TB-011, T-053, T-057). The changelog describes a randomized, idle-only backoff and new verification sessions. Each re-registration must start a fresh grant and nonce. It must not reuse stale App Attest authorization, and it must not be triggerable by a coordinator or remote party to cause churn.
- Grammar-constrained JSON for Qwen, forced tool_choice advertising, and the WebSocket upgrade 30-second timeout (TB-002). The 30-second timeout is an availability improvement. The advertised tool_constraint_models are provider-self-reported and only affect routing.
- Coordinator-state exposure in status and doctor, and the daemon state file's coordinator_connection fields. These should not leak tokens or hostnames.

The changelog is documentation, and no concrete security regression is visible in the supplied text, so there are no findings. The content is a claim about code that was not supplied. A deeper pass over the source PR is warranted for the hold socket, re-registration and delta-checkpoint paths.
